From CONFIRMED clean baseline, make the smallest possible lambda increase (+0.1, not +0.5 or +1.0). This minimal adjustment will slightly reduce overfitting by penalizing large leaf weights. The 8% train-validation gap suggests regularization is needed, but previous iterations used changes that were 5-10x too large. This conservative change should improve Top 25% by 1-2% without harming underdog performance. If underdog degrades >1%, immediately revert.

From confirmed baseline, increase min_child_weight by only 0.5 (not 1 or 2). This small increase will require slightly more samples in leaf nodes, reducing overfitting while preserving the feature interactions that underdogs depend on. Combined with lambda=1.6 from iteration 8 (if successful), this may have additive benefits. If underdog degrades >1%, immediately revert.

From confirmed baseline, add mild stochastic regularization by reducing subsample by only 0.05 (not 0.1 or 0.15). This small reduction will prevent the model from memorizing specific training patterns while maintaining stability. Sampling-based regularization is less invasive than other methods and should improve Top 25% generalization by 1-2% without affecting underdogs. If underdog degrades >1%, immediately revert.

From confirmed baseline, add mild feature sampling by reducing colsample_bytree by only 0.05. This prevents the model from relying too heavily on any single feature subset, reducing overfitting. Combined with subsample=0.95 from iteration 10 (if successful), this provides comprehensive sampling-based regularization. More conservative than previous 0.85 or 0.9 proposals. If underdog degrades >1%, immediately revert.
